note: Principles of Accounts round 1 (part B): stock valuation (FIFO/LIFO/average), control accounts, incomplete records, manufacturing accounts, not-for-profit organisations, departmental and branch accounts, partnership accounts (appropriation, goodwill, admission, dissolution), company accounts (share issues, debentures, reserves), public sector accounting, IT in accounting and ratio analysis - with a stock-movement table, a debtors' control case, a statement-of-affairs case, a manufacturing cost table, a club's receipts and payments, a partnership appropriation, a share issue, a local government budget and a two-department table as data passages.

passages.title: Stock movements of Product X
passages.text:

passages.title: Tunde's position at the start and end of 2025
passages.text:
Tunde, a trader, does not keep proper
books of account. His assets and
liabilities were:

Item              1 Jan 2025   31 Dec 2025
Stock                 80,000        95,000
Debtors               45,000        60,000
Cash at bank          25,000        15,000
Furniture (cost)     100,000       100,000
Creditors             30,000        40,000

Furniture is to be depreciated by 10% for
2025. During the year Tunde withdrew
₦120,000 for private use and paid ₦50,000
of his own money into the business as
additional capital.

passages.title: Ade and Bisi in partnership
passages.text:
Ade and Bisi are in partnership sharing
profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Their
partnership agreement provides for
interest on capital at 5% per annum, a
salary of ₦120,000 per annum for Bisi, and
interest on drawings. For the year ended
31 December 2025:

Item                    Ade        Bisi
Capital account     600,000     400,000
Interest on drawings 10,000       6,000

The net profit for the year before any
appropriation was ₦500,000.

passages.title: Share issue by Zenith Foods Plc
passages.text: Zenith Foods Plc has an authorised share capital of 10,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each. In 2025 the company offered 6,000,000 of the shares to the public at ₦1.50 per share, payable in full on application. Applications were received for 7,500,000 shares. The directors allotted 6,000,000 shares and refunded the money on the excess applications. The company also issued ₦2,000,000 of 10% debentures at par.

passages.text:
Crown Stores has two departments, A and B.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The number of units of Product X in stock on 31 January 2026 was
questions.explanation: 100 + 200 − 150 + 100 − 150 = 100 units remained at the end of the month.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Using the FIFO method, the value of the closing stock of Product X was
questions.explanation: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 100 units left are the latest purchase at ₦70 each = ₦7,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Using the LIFO method (perpetual), the value of the closing stock of Product X was
questions.explanation: Jan 15 issue takes 150 units at ₦60; Jan 28 issue takes 100 at ₦70 and 50 at ₦60. The 100 units left are the opening stock at ₦50 = ₦5,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Using the simple weighted average of all units received in the month, the value of the closing stock of Product X was
questions.explanation: Total cost = 100×50 + 200×60 + 100×70 = 24,000 for 400 units, an average of ₦60 per unit; 100 units × ₦60 = ₦6,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The gross profit on Product X for January 2026 under the FIFO method was
questions.explanation: Sales 300 units × ₦100 = 30,000; cost of goods sold = total cost 24,000 − closing stock 7,000 = 17,000; gross profit = ₦13,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a period of rising prices such as January 2026, the method that gives Product X the lowest closing stock value and the lowest gross profit is
questions.explanation: LIFO charges the latest, dearest units against sales, leaving the oldest, cheapest units in stock; profit and stock are therefore lowest.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The balance of the sales ledger control account of Ola Ventures on 30 June 2026 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the sales ledger control account of Ola Ventures, the dishonoured cheque of ₦12,000 is
questions.A: credited because the customer has paid
questions.C: ignored because it concerns the bank only
questions.D: debited because the customer's debt is restored
questions.explanation: A bounced cheque cancels the earlier receipt; the customer owes the money again, so the control account is debited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total of the debit side of the sales ledger control account of Ola Ventures for June 2026 was
questions.explanation: Opening balance 210,000 + credit sales 640,000 + dishonoured cheque 12,000 = ₦862,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The set-off of ₦8,000 in the Ola Ventures records arose because
questions.A: a customer returned goods that had been invoiced to him in error
questions.B: a debt owed by a customer who had died was written off
questions.C: the bank charged commission on cheques lodged during the month
questions.D: a customer is also a supplier and the amounts owed were netted
questions.explanation: A contra (set-off) transfers the balance owed by a person who is both a debtor and a creditor from one ledger to the other; it is credited in the sales ledger control account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which item from the Ola Ventures data would NOT be entered in the sales ledger control account?
questions.explanation: Cash purchases involve neither debtors nor creditors; every other item changes what customers owe.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Tunde's capital on 1 January 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Tunde's capital on 31 December 2025, after depreciating the furniture, was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Tunde's net profit for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Profit = closing capital 220,000 − opening capital 220,000 + drawings 120,000 − capital introduced 50,000 = ₦70,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The method used to find Tunde's profit from his opening and closing positions is called the
questions.explanation: Where no records of transactions exist, profit is deduced from the increase in net worth adjusted for drawings and capital introduced.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: If Tunde had withdrawn nothing during 2025 and introduced no capital, his closing capital would have been
questions.explanation: Closing capital would be opening capital 220,000 + profit 70,000 = ₦290,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cost of raw materials consumed by Bright Soap Factory in 2025 was
questions.explanation: Opening 40,000 + purchases 300,000 + carriage 10,000 − closing 50,000 = ₦300,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The prime cost of Bright Soap Factory for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Prime cost = raw materials consumed 300,000 + direct wages 180,000 + direct expenses 20,000 = ₦500,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total factory overheads of Bright Soap Factory for 2025 amounted to
questions.explanation: Indirect wages 60,000 + factory rent 45,000 + depreciation of plant 25,000 = ₦130,000. Office salaries are an administrative expense.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cost of goods manufactured (production cost of finished goods) by Bright Soap Factory in 2025 was
questions.explanation: Prime cost 500,000 + factory overheads 130,000 + opening WIP 30,000 − closing WIP 20,000 = ₦640,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the accounts of Bright Soap Factory the office salaries of ₦70,000 are charged to the
questions.A: manufacturing account as a factory overhead
questions.B: trading account as part of cost of sales
questions.C: profit and loss account as an administrative expense
questions.D: balance sheet as a current liability
questions.explanation: Only factory costs go into the manufacturing account; office and selling costs belong in the profit and loss account.

questions.q: The subscription income of Unity Social Club to be credited to the income and expenditure account for 2025 is

questions.q: The profit on the bar of Unity Social Club for 2025 was

questions.q: The cash balance of Unity Social Club on 31 December 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Ignoring depreciation, the surplus of income over expenditure of Unity Social Club for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Income: subscriptions 455,000 + bar profit 80,000 = 535,000. Expenditure: rent 100,000 + honorarium 40,000 = 140,000. Surplus = ₦395,000. The chairs are capital expenditure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the balance sheet of Unity Social Club at 31 December 2025, the ₦30,000 subscriptions received for 2026 are shown as
questions.explanation: Subscriptions received in advance are owed (in membership benefits) to the members and are a liability at the year end.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total interest on capital credited to Ade and Bisi for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The profit of Ade and Bisi available for sharing in the profit-sharing ratio for 2025 was
questions.explanation: 500,000 + interest on drawings 16,000 − interest on capital 50,000 − Bisi's salary 120,000 = ₦346,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Ade's share of the residual profit for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Bisi's total earnings from the partnership for 2025, net of interest on drawings, were
questions.explanation: Interest on capital 20,000 + salary 120,000 + share of profit 2/5 × 346,000 = 138,400, less interest on drawings 6,000 = ₦272,400.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the partnership of Ade and Bisi, interest on drawings is
questions.B: debited to the profit and loss account as an expense
questions.explanation: Interest charged on partners' drawings is income of the firm: it is credited to the appropriation account and debited to the partners' current accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: After the 2025 issue, the issued share capital of Zenith Foods Plc was
questions.explanation: Issued capital is recorded at nominal value: 6,000,000 shares × ₦1 = ₦6,000,000. The extra 50 kobo per share is share premium.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The share premium account of Zenith Foods Plc arising from the issue was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The amount refunded by Zenith Foods Plc to unsuccessful applicants was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The annual interest payable by Zenith Foods Plc on its debentures is
questions.explanation: 10% of ₦2,000,000 = ₦200,000, charged in the profit and loss account whether or not a profit is made.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The unissued share capital of Zenith Foods Plc after the issue was
questions.explanation: Authorised 10,000,000 shares − issued 6,000,000 shares = 4,000,000 shares of ₦1 = ₦4,000,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The debenture holders of Zenith Foods Plc differ from its ordinary shareholders in that debenture holders
questions.A: receive dividends only when profits are made
questions.B: are the last to be paid if the company is wound up
questions.C: have voting rights at the annual general meeting
questions.D: are creditors of the company entitled to fixed interest
questions.explanation: Debentures are loans: holders are creditors who receive fixed interest and rank before shareholders on winding up; they do not vote.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total budgeted revenue of the local government for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The budgeted recurrent expenditure of the local government for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure = personnel costs 500 + overhead costs 300 = ₦800 million; capital projects are capital expenditure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The budgeted overall surplus of the local government for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Total revenue 1,300 − total expenditure (800 + 450 = 1,250) = ₦50 million.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the local government budget, the statutory allocation represents
questions.D: the local government's share of the Federation Account
questions.explanation: Statutory allocations are the constitutionally fixed shares of federally collected revenue distributed to the three tiers of government.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which item in the local government budget is classified as capital expenditure?
questions.explanation: Spending on roads, buildings and other long-lived assets is capital expenditure; salaries and overheads are recurrent.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The gross profit of Department A of Crown Stores for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The gross profit of Department B of Crown Stores for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The rent charged to Department B of Crown Stores was
questions.explanation: Rent is shared 3:2 on floor area, so Department B bears 2/5 × 100,000 = ₦40,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The salaries charged to Department A of Crown Stores were
questions.explanation: Salaries are apportioned on sales 600:400 = 3:2, so Department A bears 3/5 × 90,000 = ₦54,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The net profit of Department A of Crown Stores for 2025 was
questions.explanation: Gross profit 240,000 − rent 60,000 − salaries 54,000 = ₦126,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Under the FIFO method of stock valuation, closing stock is made up of the
questions.explanation: First in, first out assumes the oldest units are sold first, so what remains is the latest bought.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Closing stock is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value in obedience to the
questions.explanation: Prudence requires that stock is not carried above the amount it is expected to realise.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Net realisable value of stock is
questions.A: the original purchase price plus carriage
questions.B: the replacement cost on the balance sheet date
questions.C: the expected selling price less costs still to be incurred to sell it
questions.D: the insured value of the goods
questions.explanation: NRV = estimated selling price − further costs of completion and selling.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An overstatement of closing stock in 2025 will
questions.A: understate the profit of 2025 and overstate the profit of 2026
questions.B: have no effect on the profit of either year
questions.C: overstate the profits of both 2025 and 2026
questions.D: overstate the profit of 2025 and understate the profit of 2026
questions.explanation: Closing stock reduces cost of sales in 2025 (profit up) and becomes the opening stock of 2026 (profit down); the error cancels over two years.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader bought 500 units at ₦40 and later 300 units at ₦50. He sold 600 units. Under FIFO the cost of goods sold was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader bought 500 units at ₦40 and later 300 units at ₦50 and sold 600 units. Under LIFO the closing stock was
questions.explanation: LIFO issues the 300 dearer units first, then 300 of the ₦40 units, leaving 200 × ₦40 = ₦8,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Opening stock 200 units at ₦30; purchases 400 units at ₦36 and 400 units at ₦45; 700 units were sold. Using the weighted average cost of all units, closing stock is valued at
questions.explanation: Total cost = 6,000 + 14,400 + 18,000 = 38,400 for 1,000 units, an average of ₦38.40 per unit; the 300 units left are valued at 300 × 38.40 = ₦11,520.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The method of stock valuation that is not permitted under International Financial Reporting Standards is
questions.explanation: IAS 2 prohibits LIFO because it can carry stock at outdated costs; FIFO, weighted average and specific identification are allowed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which method of stock valuation is most suitable for a car dealer who can trace the cost of each vehicle?
questions.explanation: When individual items are large, distinct and traceable, each is valued at its own actual cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Stock-taking is the
questions.A: recording of purchases in the day book
questions.B: sale of slow-moving goods at a discount
questions.C: physical counting and listing of goods on hand at a date
questions.explanation: A physical count at the year end establishes the quantities to be valued as closing stock.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Goods costing ₦20,000 were sent to a customer on sale or return and had not been accepted by the year end. At the year end these goods should be
questions.A: excluded from stock and treated as a sale
questions.B: written off as a bad debt
questions.C: included in stock at selling price
questions.D: included in the seller's closing stock at cost
questions.explanation: Until the customer accepts them the goods still belong to the seller and remain part of his stock at cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's closing stock at cost was ₦300,000, but an item costing ₦40,000 could only be sold for ₦28,000. Stock should be valued at
questions.explanation: The damaged item is reduced from 40,000 to its NRV of 28,000, a fall of 12,000; stock = 300,000 − 12,000 = ₦288,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: During a period of rising prices, the method that reports the highest closing stock value is
questions.explanation: FIFO leaves the most recently bought, dearest units in stock.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cost of stock includes
questions.A: the profit margin the business expects to earn on its sale
questions.B: the selling and distribution costs expected when it is sold
questions.C: the purchase price and costs of bringing it to its present location
questions.D: the cost of abnormal wastage and idle time in the factory
questions.explanation: Cost comprises purchase price, import duties, carriage inwards and conversion costs; selling costs are excluded.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cost of stock destroyed by fire in a warehouse is
questions.A: included in closing stock at its full cost
questions.B: deducted from the sales figure for the year
questions.C: added to the purchases figure for the year
questions.D: charged as a loss in the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Destroyed goods no longer exist at the year end; their cost (less any insurance recovery) is written off as a loss.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A sales ledger control account is also called a
questions.explanation: It summarises all the personal accounts of debtors in the sales ledger.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main purpose of control accounts is to
questions.A: replace the sales and purchases ledgers so that personal accounts are no longer needed
questions.B: record the cash and bank transactions of the business in summary form
questions.C: calculate the gross profit of the business without preparing a trading account
questions.D: check the arithmetical accuracy of the sales and purchases ledgers and locate errors quickly
questions.explanation: The control account balance should equal the total of the individual ledger balances; any difference signals an error in that ledger.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is entered on the credit side of the purchases ledger control account?
questions.explanation: Credit purchases increase the amount owed to suppliers, so they are credited; the other three reduce the liability and are debited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following appears on the debit side of the sales ledger control account?
questions.explanation: Credit sales increase debtors and are debited; receipts, discounts and returns reduce debtors and are credited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The source of the credit sales figure in the sales ledger control account is the
questions.C: total of the sales day book
questions.explanation: Control accounts are built from the totals of the books of original entry, not from the personal accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Opening creditors ₦150,000; credit purchases ₦720,000; payments to suppliers ₦650,000; discount received ₦18,000; returns outwards ₦22,000. The closing creditors balance is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A credit balance on a sales ledger control account may arise when
questions.A: goods are sold for cash to a customer who also buys on credit
questions.B: a supplier has been paid in advance for goods not yet delivered
questions.C: a customer has overpaid or paid for goods later returned
questions.D: bad debts are written off against the provision for doubtful debts
questions.explanation: Overpayments and credit notes issued after payment leave the customer as a creditor of the business.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The total of the sales ledger balances exceeds the balance on the sales ledger control account. Which error could explain the difference?
questions.A: an invoice omitted from the sales day book but posted to the customer's account
questions.C: cash received from a debtor not recorded anywhere
questions.D: a credit sale omitted from both the day book and the ledger
questions.explanation: An invoice posted to the personal account but missing from the day book total makes the ledger total larger than the control account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Bad debts written off are recorded in the sales ledger control account on the
questions.explanation: Writing off a debt reduces total debtors, so the control account is credited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Interest charged to a customer on an overdue account is
questions.A: credited to the sales ledger control account
questions.B: debited to the purchases ledger control account
questions.C: debited to the sales ledger control account
questions.explanation: Interest increases what the customer owes, so debtors (and the control account) are debited.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Discount received from suppliers is recorded in the purchases ledger control account on the
questions.explanation: Discount received reduces the amount owed to suppliers and is debited in the total creditors account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The sales ledger control account shows a balance of ₦520,000 but the list of debtors totals ₦512,000. It is then found that the sales day book was overcast by ₦8,000. After correction the
questions.A: control account balance falls to ₦512,000 and agrees with the list
questions.B: list of debtors rises to ₦520,000 and agrees with the control account
questions.C: difference between the two figures becomes ₦16,000
questions.D: control account balance rises to ₦528,000 and the difference doubles
questions.explanation: An overcast day book inflates the control account only; correcting it reduces the control balance by 8,000 to ₦512,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A provision for doubtful debts is
questions.A: entered in the sales ledger control account
questions.B: entered in the purchases ledger control account
questions.C: not entered in the sales ledger control account
questions.explanation: The provision is a general estimate kept in a separate account; it does not alter any individual debtor's balance or the control account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The person who keeps the sales ledger should not also keep the sales ledger control account because
questions.A: it would be too much work for one clerk to handle in a single day
questions.B: the auditor is required to keep the control account personally
questions.C: the control account must by law be kept by the bank on behalf of the business
questions.D: the control account is a check on the ledger and independence detects fraud and error
questions.explanation: Separating the duties makes it harder to conceal errors or misappropriation in the debtors' ledger.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cash sales are
questions.A: debited to the sales ledger control account
questions.B: credited to the sales ledger control account
questions.C: not entered in the sales ledger control account
questions.D: credited to the purchases ledger control account
questions.explanation: Only credit transactions with customers pass through the debtors' control account; cash sales create no debtor.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Single entry is a system in which
questions.A: every transaction is recorded twice, once on each side of the ledger
questions.B: only the fixed assets of the business are recorded in a register
questions.C: only some aspects of transactions, usually cash and personal accounts, are recorded
questions.D: records are kept only by limited companies and never by sole traders
questions.explanation: Small traders often keep a cash book and records of debtors and creditors without a complete double entry system.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's capital increased from ₦400,000 to ₦520,000 during a year in which he withdrew ₦90,000 and introduced no new capital. His profit for the year was
questions.explanation: Profit = increase in capital 120,000 + drawings 90,000 = ₦210,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's net assets fell from ₦300,000 to ₦280,000 during a year in which his drawings were ₦60,000 and he introduced ₦10,000 capital. His result for the year was a

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A statement of affairs is prepared under incomplete records in order to find the
questions.explanation: Listing assets and liabilities at a date gives the capital (net worth) at that date.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Opening debtors ₦50,000; cash received from debtors ₦610,000; closing debtors ₦70,000; discount allowed ₦5,000. Credit sales for the year were
questions.explanation: Credit sales = receipts 610,000 + discount 5,000 + closing debtors 70,000 − opening debtors 50,000 = ₦635,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Opening creditors ₦40,000; payments to suppliers ₦380,000; closing creditors ₦55,000. Credit purchases for the year were
questions.explanation: Purchases = payments 380,000 + closing creditors 55,000 − opening creditors 40,000 = ₦395,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's sales were ₦840,000 at a uniform mark-up of 40% on cost. Opening stock was ₦60,000 and purchases ₦620,000. Closing stock was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader's stock was destroyed by fire. Sales up to the fire were ₦450,000 at a gross margin of 20% on sales; opening stock ₦70,000; purchases ₦360,000. The cost of stock destroyed was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The conversion of single entry to double entry involves
questions.A: preparing control accounts for debtors and creditors to find credit sales and purchases
questions.B: closing down the business and selling all its assets to start afresh
questions.C: writing off all the debtors of the business as bad debts
questions.D: ignoring all the cash transactions of the business for the period
questions.explanation: Total debtors and total creditors accounts, together with the cash summary, reconstruct the missing figures.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader banked all takings after paying wages of ₦120,000 and drawings of ₦80,000 in cash. Bankings were ₦900,000. His total cash sales were
questions.explanation: Cash sales = amount banked 900,000 + cash used before banking (120,000 + 80,000) = ₦1,100,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the single entry system?
questions.A: it is cheap to operate and needs few books
questions.B: it records every transaction twice and wastes time
questions.C: a trial balance cannot be extracted so errors are hard to detect
questions.D: it needs a qualified accountant to operate it every day
questions.explanation: Without complete double entry there is no arithmetical check, and profit can only be estimated.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A trader had opening capital ₦250,000 and closing capital ₦310,000. During the year he took goods costing ₦15,000 for his family and cash of ₦45,000, and he won ₦100,000 in a lottery which he paid into the business. His profit was
questions.explanation: Profit = 60,000 increase + drawings 60,000 − capital introduced 100,000 = ₦20,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Prime cost consists of
questions.A: direct materials, direct labour and direct expenses
questions.D: direct wages and depreciation of office furniture
questions.explanation: Prime cost is the total of all direct costs of production.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a factory overhead?
questions.explanation: Supervisors' salaries are indirect labour, part of factory overheads; materials and operators' wages are direct costs.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Work in progress at the end of the year is
questions.D: ignored until the goods are finished
questions.explanation: Closing work in progress represents cost not yet turned into finished goods, so it is deducted (and opening WIP added) to arrive at the cost of goods completed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The cost of production of finished goods is transferred from the manufacturing account to the
questions.explanation: The trading account uses the cost of goods manufactured in place of purchases.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Raw materials consumed = ₦400,000; direct wages ₦250,000; royalties per unit produced ₦30,000; factory power ₦45,000. Prime cost was
questions.explanation: Royalties based on output are a direct expense: 400,000 + 250,000 + 30,000 = ₦680,000. Factory power is an overhead.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A factory transfers goods to the warehouse at cost plus 20%. Cost of production was ₦900,000. The manufacturing profit and the transfer price are
questions.explanation: 20% of 900,000 = 180,000 manufacturing profit; transfer price = ₦1,080,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a manufacturing business, the three classes of stock are
questions.A: raw materials, work in progress and finished goods
questions.explanation: Each class is valued separately at the year end and shown under current assets.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a direct expense of production?
questions.A: hire of a special machine for a particular job
questions.explanation: Costs traceable to a specific product or job are direct; rent, depreciation and management salaries are indirect.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Carriage inwards on raw materials is
questions.A: added to the cost of raw materials consumed
questions.C: charged to the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Delivery costs of materials are part of the cost of getting them to the factory, so they increase the direct materials cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Purchases of raw materials ₦500,000; returns outwards ₦20,000; opening raw materials ₦60,000; closing raw materials ₦80,000; direct wages ₦300,000; factory overheads ₦150,000; opening WIP ₦40,000; closing WIP ₦70,000. Cost of goods manufactured was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A manufacturing account is prepared to ascertain the
questions.explanation: It collects the factory costs of the period to arrive at the cost of finished goods produced.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which item appears in the profit and loss account and not in the manufacturing account of a factory?
questions.explanation: Selling costs such as commission are not costs of manufacturing; they are charged against gross profit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The reason a manufacturer may add a profit loading when transferring goods to the trading account is to
questions.A: increase the total profit of the business for the year
questions.B: value the closing stock of finished goods at selling price
questions.C: reduce the amount of tax payable on the profit of the year
questions.D: show whether it is cheaper to make the goods or to buy them from outside
questions.explanation: Transferring at market value reveals a separate manufacturing profit and lets management compare making with buying.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Finished goods are transferred at cost plus 25%. Closing stock of finished goods at transfer price is ₦250,000. The provision for unrealised profit on the closing stock is
questions.explanation: Unrealised profit = 250,000 × 25/125 = ₦50,000, which must be removed so that stock is shown at cost.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The receipts and payments account of a club is equivalent to a trader's
questions.explanation: It is a summary of the cash and bank transactions of the period, including capital items.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The income and expenditure account of a club corresponds to a trader's
questions.explanation: It matches the period's revenue income against revenue expenditure on the accrual basis to find the surplus or deficit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The excess of income over expenditure of a club is called
questions.explanation: Non-trading organisations speak of a surplus (or deficit), not profit or loss.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The capital of a club or society is usually called the
questions.explanation: The accumulated fund is the excess of assets over liabilities, built up from surpluses over the years.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Subscriptions in arrears at the year end are shown in the balance sheet of a club as
questions.explanation: Amounts owed by members are receivable by the club, hence a current asset (subject to prudence).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A one-off large donation received by a club for the building of a new hall should be
questions.A: credited to income and expenditure account
questions.B: used to pay the secretary's honorarium
questions.D: capitalised and shown as a special fund on the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Donations for a specific capital purpose are not income of the year; they are credited to a building fund.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Entrance fees of new members are usually treated as
questions.A: revenue income of the year, unless the club decides to capitalise them
questions.B: a loan to the club repayable when the member leaves
questions.C: an expense of the club charged to income and expenditure
questions.D: a deduction from the accumulated fund at the year end
questions.explanation: Small recurring entrance fees are treated as income; where they are large and non-recurring they may be capitalised.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Subscriptions received in 2025 were ₦600,000. Arrears at the start of 2025 were ₦40,000 and at the end ₦55,000; advances at the start were ₦20,000 and at the end ₦35,000. Subscription income for 2025 was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Life membership fees received by a club are best treated as
questions.A: income of the year in which they are received
questions.B: a fixed asset of the club shown in the balance sheet
questions.C: a liability to be released to income over the expected membership period
questions.D: a deduction from the expenditure of the year of receipt
questions.explanation: The member has paid in advance for many years' benefits, so the fee is spread over the estimated period.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A club's bar or canteen trading result is calculated in a
questions.A: receipts and payments account together with the other cash items
questions.B: subscription account along with the members' subscriptions
questions.C: statement of affairs prepared at the beginning of the year
questions.D: separate bar trading account whose profit is transferred to income and expenditure
questions.explanation: Trading activities are accounted for separately; only the bar profit (or loss) enters the income and expenditure account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The honorarium paid to a club secretary is
questions.A: capital expenditure added to the fixed assets
questions.B: a distribution of the surplus to one of the members
questions.C: revenue expenditure charged to the income and expenditure account
questions.D: a deduction from the subscriptions received in the year
questions.explanation: An honorarium is a payment for services to the club and is an expense of the year.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A club had an accumulated fund of ₦850,000 at the start of the year. It made a deficit of ₦60,000 and received a legacy of ₦200,000 which it capitalised. Its accumulated fund at the year end was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a not-for-profit organisation?
questions.explanation: Clubs, societies, associations and charities exist to serve their members or the public, not to earn profit for owners.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The purchase of a lawn mower by a sports club is recorded in the
questions.A: receipts and payments account and the balance sheet
questions.explanation: As a cash payment it appears in the receipts and payments account; as capital expenditure it becomes a fixed asset, with only depreciation charged to income and expenditure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Departmental accounts are prepared mainly to
questions.A: show the profit or loss made by each department separately
questions.B: reduce the total expenses of the business
questions.C: calculate the salary of the general manager
questions.D: value the closing stock of the whole business
questions.explanation: Separate results show which departments are profitable and help management decide on expansion or closure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The most suitable basis for apportioning rent between departments is
questions.C: number of employees in each department
questions.D: floor area occupied by each department
questions.explanation: Rent is a cost of space, so floor area is the fairest basis.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The most suitable basis for apportioning advertising expenses between departments is
questions.explanation: Advertising promotes sales, so the benefit is assumed to follow sales value.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Depreciation of departmental equipment is best apportioned on the basis of
questions.A: the value of the equipment in each department
questions.B: the sales made by each department
questions.C: the number of staff in each department
questions.D: the floor area occupied by each department
questions.explanation: The charge follows the asset that causes it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Electricity of ₦120,000 is to be shared among departments X, Y and Z in the ratio of floor area 5:3:2. Department Y's share is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Expenses that cannot reasonably be apportioned among departments should be
questions.B: charged to the department with the largest sales
questions.C: charged against the combined profit of all departments
questions.D: capitalised and shown as an asset
questions.explanation: Unallocable items such as the general manager's salary are deducted in the general profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Goods transferred from Department P to Department Q at cost are recorded by
questions.A: debit Department Q purchases, credit Department P purchases (or sales)
questions.D: no entry, since the goods remain in the business
questions.explanation: Inter-departmental transfers must be recorded so that each department's cost of sales and gross profit are correct.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The advantage of departmental accounts to management is that they
questions.A: eliminate the need for a balance sheet at the end of the year
questions.B: remove the need for stock-taking in each of the departments
questions.C: reduce the amount of tax payable by the business as a whole
questions.D: reveal loss-making departments so that corrective action can be taken
questions.explanation: Comparing departmental gross profit ratios highlights weak departments and helps in planning.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: When the head office keeps all the accounting records of a branch, the branch stock is usually invoiced at
questions.A: cost or selling price, as decided by head office
questions.C: the market value at the year end
questions.D: the historical cost of head office premises
questions.explanation: Goods may be sent at cost, at cost plus a fixed percentage, or at selling price to control the branch.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Goods are sent to a branch at cost plus 25%. Goods invoiced to the branch amounted to ₦500,000. The cost of these goods was

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main purpose of invoicing goods to a branch at selling price is to
questions.A: increase the profit reported by the branch
questions.B: avoid paying tax on the sales made by the branch
questions.C: reduce the price paid by customers of the branch
questions.D: enable head office to check the branch stock and detect losses
questions.explanation: Since all sales should be at the invoice price, any difference between expected and actual stock reveals shortages or pilferage.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A branch receives goods invoiced at selling price. Opening stock ₦60,000, goods received ₦540,000, sales ₦520,000, closing stock ₦70,000 (all at selling price). The stock shortage was
questions.explanation: Expected closing stock = 60,000 + 540,000 − 520,000 = 80,000; actual 70,000; shortage ₦10,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the head office books, the branch stock account is
questions.A: a real account showing stock held at the branch
questions.B: a personal account of the branch manager
questions.C: a nominal account for branch expenses
questions.explanation: Branch stock account records the goods held at the branch (at cost or invoice price).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Where goods are sent to a branch at cost plus a mark-up, the unrealised profit in closing branch stock is
questions.A: credited to the branch adjustment account and carried forward
questions.B: treated as part of the branch profit for the year
questions.C: added to the sales figure of the head office
questions.D: written off as a bad debt in the head office books
questions.explanation: The loading on unsold stock has not been realised, so it is kept back in the branch adjustment (mark-up) account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cash remitted by a branch to head office is recorded in the head office books by
questions.explanation: Head office receives cash (debit bank) and the branch's indebtedness falls (credit branch account).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A branch that keeps its own complete set of books records goods received from head office by
questions.A: debit goods from head office (purchases), credit head office current account
questions.B: debit head office current account, credit branch sales account
questions.C: debit cash account, credit goods from head office (purchases)
questions.D: debit head office current account, credit bank account
questions.explanation: The head office current account in the branch books shows what the branch owes head office.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: At the year end the head office current account in the branch books shows ₦900,000 while the branch current account in the head office books shows ₦950,000. The difference is most likely due to
questions.A: cash or goods in transit between the two
questions.B: an error in the branch stock count
questions.explanation: Items sent by one party but not yet received and recorded by the other create temporary differences that must be reconciled.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Branch accounts differ from departmental accounts in that a branch
questions.A: is located away from the head office
questions.B: sells only to the head office
questions.C: has no stock of its own
questions.explanation: Departments operate under one roof; branches are geographically separate outlets or units of the same business.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared
questions.B: in proportion to time spent in the business
questions.explanation: The Partnership Act provides for equal sharing where the partners have not agreed otherwise.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the absence of a partnership agreement, a loan by a partner to the firm attracts interest at
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act a partner is entitled to 5% per annum on advances beyond his agreed capital, but no interest on capital and no salary.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Interest on partners' capital is provided in order to
questions.A: reward the partners for the work they do in the firm
questions.B: increase the total profit of the firm for the year
questions.C: compensate partners fairly when capital contributions differ
questions.D: reduce the tax payable by the partners on their shares
questions.explanation: Without it, a partner who contributes more capital would be disadvantaged if profits were shared in some other ratio.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A partner's salary is
questions.A: an expense charged in the profit and loss account
questions.C: a drawing debited to the capital account
questions.D: an appropriation of profit debited in the appropriation account
questions.explanation: Salaries to partners are a way of dividing profit, not a cost of earning it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Where fixed capital accounts are kept, a partner's share of profit, salary and interest are credited to his
questions.explanation: Fixed capital accounts change only when capital is introduced or withdrawn; all other entries go through current accounts.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A debit balance on a partner's current account means that the partner
questions.A: has drawn more than his total entitlement
questions.B: has undrawn profits in the firm
questions.C: owns more capital than the others
questions.D: has lent money to the firm
questions.explanation: The partner has overdrawn his share of profits, salary and interest and effectively owes the firm.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: X and Y share profits 2:1. Net profit was ₦360,000 after charging interest of ₦20,000 on a loan from X. Interest on capital was ₦30,000 for X and ₦15,000 for Y. X's total income from the firm for the year was
questions.explanation: Residual = 360,000 − 45,000 = 315,000; X's share 2/3 = 210,000; plus interest on capital 30,000 and loan interest 20,000 = ₦260,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Goodwill is created in the books when a new partner is admitted in order to
questions.A: give the new partner a share of the profits earned before he joined
questions.B: reduce the capital accounts of the old partners to the level of the new one
questions.C: increase the cash resources of the firm at the date of admission
questions.D: compensate the old partners for the share of the firm's reputation the new partner will enjoy
questions.explanation: Goodwill built up by the old partners is credited to them in the old ratio before the new partner shares in future profits.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A and B share profits 3:2. They admit C who takes a one-fifth share. Goodwill is valued at ₦200,000 and is not to remain in the books. The net effect on A's capital account is
questions.A: a credit of ₦120,000 and a debit of ₦96,000
questions.D: a credit of ₦96,000 and a debit of ₦120,000
questions.explanation: Goodwill raised is credited in the old ratio (A 3/5 × 200,000 = 120,000); written off in the new ratio A:B:C = 12:8:5, A bears 12/25 × 200,000 = 96,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: On admission of a new partner, the revaluation of assets is carried out so that
questions.A: the new partner can buy his share of the assets at a cheaper price
questions.B: the firm can pay less tax on the profit of the year of admission
questions.C: profits or losses on assets up to the date of admission accrue only to the old partners
questions.D: the bank can grant a loan on the security of the revalued assets
questions.explanation: Increases or decreases in asset values before admission belong to the old partners in the old ratio.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The document that sets out the rights and duties of partners is the
questions.explanation: The partnership deed (agreement) covers capital, profit sharing, salaries, interest and admission or retirement of partners.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: On the dissolution of a partnership, the account opened to record the sale of assets and settlement of liabilities is the
questions.explanation: Assets are transferred to the realisation account at book value; proceeds and expenses are recorded there and the balance is the profit or loss on realisation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: On dissolution, after all assets are realised and creditors paid, a partner's capital account shows a debit balance of ₦50,000 and he is insolvent. Under the rule in Garner v Murray the deficiency is borne by the solvent partners
questions.B: in the ratio of their last agreed capitals
questions.D: by the partner with the largest drawings
questions.explanation: Garner v Murray requires solvent partners to bear an insolvent partner's deficiency in the ratio of their capitals before dissolution.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT usually found in a partnership appropriation account?
questions.explanation: Interest on a partner's loan is a charge against profit in the profit and loss account, not an appropriation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The maximum number of partners in an ordinary trading partnership in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Ordinary partnerships are limited to 20 members; beyond that a company must be formed (professional firms are exempt).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares profit but takes no part in management is a
questions.explanation: A sleeping partner invests but does not manage; a nominal partner lends only his name.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Partners P and Q share profits 3:1. Q is guaranteed a minimum of ₦150,000 per year. Profit for the year was ₦480,000. P's share after honouring the guarantee was
questions.explanation: Normal shares: P 360,000, Q 120,000. Q's shortfall of 30,000 is made up by P, leaving P with ₦330,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The document that states the objects of a company and its authorised share capital is the
questions.explanation: The memorandum defines the company's name, objects and capital; the articles regulate its internal management.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The maximum amount of share capital a company is allowed to issue is its
questions.explanation: Authorised (registered or nominal) capital is the ceiling stated in the memorandum.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The part of the called-up capital that shareholders have actually paid is the
questions.explanation: Paid-up capital = called-up capital − calls in arrears.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: When shares are issued at a price above their nominal value, the excess is credited to
questions.explanation: Share premium is a capital reserve that cannot be distributed as dividend.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Shareholders who receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders hold
questions.explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend and rank before ordinary shares for dividend and usually for repayment of capital.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cumulative preference shares differ from non-cumulative preference shares in that
questions.A: unpaid dividends are carried forward and must be paid before ordinary dividends
questions.B: they carry voting rights at every general meeting of the company
questions.C: they are always redeemable at the option of the company
questions.D: their dividend varies with the profits earned each year
questions.explanation: Arrears of cumulative preference dividend accumulate until paid.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Debenture interest is
questions.A: an appropriation of profit decided by the shareholders
questions.B: a charge against profit payable whether or not profits are made
questions.C: paid only when the directors recommend it at the year end
questions.D: the same as a dividend on ordinary shares
questions.explanation: Debentures are loans; their interest is an expense in the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Bonus shares are issued
questions.A: for cash at a premium to the public
questions.B: free to existing shareholders out of reserves
questions.C: to debenture holders in place of interest
questions.D: to employees only as part of their pay
questions.explanation: A bonus (capitalisation) issue converts reserves into share capital without bringing in cash.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A rights issue is an offer of new shares
questions.A: to the general public at a premium through a prospectus issued by the directors
questions.B: to existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings, usually at a favourable price
questions.C: to the directors only as a reward for their services
questions.D: to the government in exchange for a licence to operate
questions.explanation: Rights issues raise cash from existing shareholders and preserve their proportionate ownership.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company has 5,000,000 ordinary shares of 50k each and 1,000,000 8% preference shares of ₦1 each. Profit available for distribution is ₦900,000. If the directors pay the preference dividend and an ordinary dividend of 10k per share, the retained profit is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company's retained earnings appear in the balance sheet as part of
questions.explanation: Retained profits belong to the shareholders and are shown with share capital and reserves.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The dividend proposed by directors but not yet approved by shareholders at the year end is
questions.A: shown as a current liability in the balance sheet
questions.B: disclosed in a note and not recognised as a liability
questions.C: deducted from the share capital of the company
questions.D: credited to the share premium account
questions.explanation: Under IFRS a proposed dividend becomes a liability only when declared (approved), so at the year end it is disclosed but not accrued.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Calls in arrears are
questions.A: deducted from called-up capital to give paid-up capital
questions.B: added to the share premium account of the company
questions.C: shown as a current liability in the balance sheet
questions.D: written off to the profit and loss account of the year
questions.explanation: Amounts called but not yet paid by shareholders reduce the paid-up capital figure.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company issued 2,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 at ₦1.20, payable ₦0.50 on application (including the premium), ₦0.40 on allotment and ₦0.30 on first and final call. The amount credited to share premium account was
questions.explanation: Premium = (1.20 − 1.00) × 2,000,000 = ₦400,000, received with the application money.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a capital reserve?
questions.explanation: Capital reserves (share premium, capital redemption reserve, revaluation reserve) are not available for cash dividends; the others are revenue reserves.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main advantage of a limited liability company over a partnership is that
questions.A: it pays no tax on the profits it earns
questions.B: shareholders' liability is limited to the amount unpaid on their shares
questions.C: it needs no audit of its annual accounts
questions.D: profits are shared equally among all the shareholders
questions.explanation: Members of a limited company cannot be called upon to pay the company's debts beyond their shareholding.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The statement that must be prepared by a company showing its assets, liabilities and equity at the year end is the
questions.explanation: The statement of financial position is the IFRS name for the balance sheet.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company redeemed ₦1,000,000 of preference shares out of profits. To protect creditors, an amount equal to the nominal value redeemed must be transferred to
questions.explanation: The capital redemption reserve keeps the company's permanent capital intact when shares are redeemed out of distributable profits.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Preliminary (formation) expenses of a company are normally
questions.A: capitalised as a fixed asset and depreciated
questions.B: written off against share premium or profit in the first year
questions.C: added to the share capital of the company
questions.D: treated as a current asset for as long as the company exists
questions.explanation: Formation costs have no lasting value and are written off, share premium being one permitted source.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Persons who manage the affairs of a company on behalf of the shareholders are the
questions.explanation: Directors are elected by shareholders to run the company and are accountable to them.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Government accounting in Nigeria is mainly based on the
questions.explanation: Public sector accounts have traditionally recorded revenue when received and expenditure when paid, though IPSAS accrual accounting is being adopted.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The account into which all revenues of the Federal Government are paid, as required by the Constitution, is the
questions.explanation: Section 80 of the 1999 Constitution establishes the Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The account from which federally collected revenue is shared among the federal, state and local governments is the
questions.explanation: Revenue such as oil receipts, companies income tax and customs duties is paid into the Federation Account for distribution by the approved formula.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The officer of the Federal Government who audits and reports on the public accounts to the National Assembly is the
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General is independent of the executive and reports to the legislature.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The officer responsible for keeping the accounts of the Federal Government and preparing the annual financial statements is the
questions.D: Chairman of the Revenue Mobilisation Commission
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General heads the Treasury and is the chief accounting officer of receipts and payments.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The document that authorises government expenditure for a year is the
questions.explanation: The budget becomes law as the Appropriation Act once passed by the legislature and assented to.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Personnel costs, overheads and debt servicing are examples of government
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure is spent on running the government year after year; capital expenditure creates lasting assets.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A vote in government accounting is
questions.A: an election held among civil servants to choose a treasurer
questions.B: an amount approved by the legislature for a specific purpose
questions.C: a warrant signed by the Auditor-General for the Federation
questions.D: the balance standing in the Federation Account at the year end
questions.explanation: Money can only be spent under the head and sub-head (vote) for which it was appropriated.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A ministry spent money on a project not provided for in the Appropriation Act. This is known as
questions.explanation: Spending outside the approved budget is unauthorised (extra-budgetary); a supplementary appropriation is the lawful route.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Virement in public sector accounting means
questions.A: the transfer of savings from one sub-head to another within the same head with approval
questions.B: the audit of government accounts by the Auditor-General at the end of the year
questions.C: the sharing of the Federation Account among the three tiers of government
questions.D: the collection of taxes by agents appointed by the revenue authorities
questions.explanation: Virement allows limited re-allocation of funds without a new Appropriation Act.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The authority issued by the Minister of Finance to the Accountant-General permitting the release of funds is a
questions.explanation: Warrants (e.g. the Annual General Warrant) authorise expenditure from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The book kept by a ministry to record its expenditure against the amounts allocated in the budget is the
questions.explanation: The vote book shows the balance remaining on each vote so that expenditure is not exceeded.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) introduced in Nigeria requires that
questions.A: all government revenues are paid into a unified account at the Central Bank
questions.B: every ministry keeps its own commercial bank accounts
questions.C: local governments pay revenue to state governments
questions.D: taxes are paid only in cash
questions.explanation: TSA consolidates government cash balances in one account at the CBN to improve control and transparency.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The international standards on which Nigeria's public sector accounting reforms are based are the
questions.explanation: IPSAS, issued by the IPSAS Board, guide accrual-based financial reporting by governments.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Personal income tax paid by workers in a state is collected by the
questions.explanation: PAYE of residents is a state revenue collected by the State Board of Internal Revenue.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main source of revenue for most Nigerian local governments is
questions.B: statutory allocation from the Federation Account
questions.explanation: Most local governments depend heavily on their monthly statutory allocations.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The fund from which unforeseen and urgent expenditure may be met pending approval by the legislature is the
questions.explanation: Advances from the Contingencies Fund are later replaced by a supplementary appropriation.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In the public sector, the accounting officer of a ministry, answerable for its funds, is usually the
questions.explanation: The Permanent Secretary is the accounting officer and can be summoned by the Public Accounts Committee.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The main purpose of public sector accounting is to
questions.A: maximise the profit earned by the government each year
questions.B: demonstrate stewardship and accountability for public funds
questions.C: reduce the salaries and allowances of civil servants
questions.D: increase the amount the nation can borrow abroad
questions.explanation: Governments account to the legislature and the public for how money voted was spent.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A payment voucher in government accounting must be supported by
questions.A: the personal opinion of the cashier that the payment is genuine
questions.B: documents such as invoices, receipts and evidence of approval
questions.C: a newspaper advertisement announcing the payment
questions.D: a bank statement of the payee for the previous six months
questions.explanation: Every payment must be properly authorised and supported before the Treasury will pass it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A computerised accounting system differs from a manual one mainly in that it
questions.A: does not use the double entry principle at all
questions.B: processes and posts transactions automatically once entered
questions.C: requires no source documents to support entries
questions.D: cannot produce a trial balance at the end of a period
questions.explanation: Once a transaction is captured, the software posts to the ledger, updates balances and produces reports instantly; double entry still underlies it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A program in which figures are arranged in rows and columns and formulae recalculate totals automatically is a
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets such as Microsoft Excel are widely used for budgets, schedules and financial analysis.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of computerised accounting?
questions.A: it eliminates the need for internal control
questions.B: speed and accuracy in processing large volumes of transactions
questions.explanation: Computers process data quickly and consistently, but controls, backups and training are still needed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of computerised accounting?
questions.A: reports are produced quickly at the end of the period
questions.B: risk of data loss through virus attack or system failure
questions.C: arithmetical errors in posting and balancing are reduced
questions.D: records take much less storage space than paper ledgers
questions.explanation: Dependence on hardware and software exposes the records to viruses, power failure and hacking, hence the need for backups.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The physical components of a computer such as the keyboard, monitor and processor are called
questions.explanation: Hardware is the tangible equipment; software is the set of programs that run on it.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is accounting software?
questions.explanation: Sage, QuickBooks, Peachtree and Tally are widely used accounting packages.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The sequence of processing in a computerised accounting system is
questions.explanation: Data is entered (input), processed by the program, stored, and reports are produced (output).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Making a copy of accounting data on a separate device or in the cloud so that it can be restored after a failure is called
questions.explanation: Regular backups protect against loss of records through hardware failure, theft or virus attack.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A password in an accounting package is used to
questions.A: speed up the processing of data
questions.explanation: Access controls are an internal control that prevents unauthorised entry or alteration of records.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Garbage in, garbage out (GIGO) means that
questions.A: computers produce wrong output if the input data is wrong
questions.B: computers must be cleaned regularly to avoid breakdown
questions.C: old computers should be discarded and replaced with new ones
questions.D: printers waste paper when reports are printed too often
questions.explanation: The computer cannot correct inaccurate or incomplete data entered by users.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An audit trail in a computerised system is
questions.A: the auditor's travelling expenses when visiting the branches of a client
questions.B: a record that allows a transaction to be traced from source document to final report
questions.C: a list of the auditor's staff and the work assigned to each of them
questions.D: the fee charged by the auditor for examining the computerised records
questions.explanation: An audit trail shows who entered what and when, so that figures in the accounts can be verified back to their origin.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Electronic banking allows a business to
questions.A: avoid keeping a cash book because the bank keeps all the records
questions.B: transfer funds, pay suppliers and check balances online without visiting the bank
questions.C: stop reconciling its bank account because the statement is always correct
questions.D: borrow money from the bank without paying any interest on the loan
questions.explanation: Internet and mobile banking speed up payments and collections; records and reconciliations remain necessary.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A company keeps its accounting records on servers it accesses over the internet rather than on its own computers. This arrangement is called
questions.explanation: Cloud-based accounting packages store data remotely and allow access from any location.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The device used to produce a printed copy of a financial statement is the
questions.explanation: A printer produces hard copy output; a scanner captures images as input.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: In a spreadsheet, the formula =SUM(B2:B10) will
questions.A: multiply the values in B2 and B10
questions.B: add all the values from cell B2 to cell B10
questions.C: find the average of B2 to B10
questions.D: count the empty cells in column B
questions.explanation: SUM adds the values in the specified range of cells.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: An Automated Teller Machine (ATM) card used to pay for goods directly from the buyer's bank balance is a
questions.explanation: A debit card draws immediately on funds in the customer's account; a credit card draws on a line of credit.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A firm records sales during the day and posts them all to the ledger at night in one run. This method of processing is called
questions.explanation: Batch processing accumulates transactions and processes them together at intervals; real-time systems update records immediately.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following is an internal control in a computerised accounting system?
questions.A: allowing all staff to use one password
questions.B: separating the duties of data entry and authorisation
questions.C: disabling the audit trail to save space
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties, access levels and audit trails reduce the risk of fraud and error.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The current ratio is calculated as
questions.explanation: It measures the ability of a business to meet its short-term obligations.

questions.q: A current ratio of 0.8 : 1 indicates that the business
questions.A: has more current assets than current liabilities
questions.B: may have difficulty paying its short-term debts
questions.explanation: Current liabilities exceed current assets, a sign of possible liquidity problems.

questions.q: Net profit ₦300,000; capital employed ₦1,500,000. Return on capital employed is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The rate of stock turnover measures
questions.A: how many times average stock is sold and replaced in a period
questions.B: the gross profit earned on each unit of stock sold in the period
questions.C: the number of days that credit customers take to pay their accounts
questions.D: the ratio of the fixed assets of the business to its sales
questions.explanation: Stock turnover = cost of goods sold ÷ average stock; a higher figure usually means faster-moving stock.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Average stock ₦80,000; stock turnover 6 times; gross margin 25% on sales. Sales for the year were

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A fall in the gross profit percentage from one year to the next may be caused by
questions.A: an increase in the rent paid for the shop
questions.B: selling goods at lower prices without a fall in cost
questions.C: an increase in the salaries paid to the sales staff
questions.D: higher advertising costs in the second year
questions.explanation: Gross profit percentage is affected only by trading account items such as selling prices, purchase costs and stock losses.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A business has fixed assets ₦800,000, current assets ₦300,000, current liabilities ₦150,000 and a long-term loan of ₦250,000. Its capital employed (owner's equity) is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: The ratio that measures how much of a company's long-term finance is provided by borrowing rather than by shareholders is the
questions.explanation: Gearing (leverage) compares fixed-interest capital with equity; high gearing means greater risk to ordinary shareholders.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Which of the following users would be most interested in the liquidity ratios of a business?
questions.A: a trade creditor deciding whether to supply goods on credit
questions.B: a customer buying one item for cash
questions.explanation: Suppliers want assurance that the business can pay its short-term debts as they fall due.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Purchases on credit ₦730,000; average creditors ₦60,000. The average payment period (365 days) is

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A business has a current ratio of 2 : 1 and current liabilities of ₦300,000. It then pays a creditor ₦100,000 by cheque. The new current ratio is
questions.explanation: Current assets were 600,000. After payment: 500,000 ÷ 200,000 = 2.5 : 1.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Earnings per share is calculated as
questions.A: profit after tax and preference dividend ÷ number of ordinary shares
questions.B: total dividend paid in the year ÷ number of shareholders on the register
questions.C: sales for the year ÷ number of ordinary shares in issue
questions.D: market price of the share ÷ dividend per share for the year
questions.explanation: EPS shows the profit earned for each ordinary share and is a key measure for investors.
